title: Physical activity after proximal femur fracture - course and correlation with individual functionality at the end of the inpatient stay
summary: Patients are contacted by the study physician after their surgery to inform them about the study. They are given 24 hours to consider their options and if they provide informed consent, they are included in the study. A study assistant from the Department of Geriatrics then performs tests with the patients that are not part of routine data, both shortly before discharge and after surgery. These tests do not include those marked as "patient record" in Table 1. Additionally, the study assistant places an ActivPAL sensor on the patient's non-operated thigh, covering it with a waterproof plaster. The sensor can be worn continuously for seven days, including during showering and sleeping. However, patients have the option to remove the sensor at any time. In addition, participants are contacted by telephone six months after discharge to complete another questionnaire on physical activity.

interventions.name: A total of 70 patients with proximal femur fracture in the Geriatric Traumatology Center of Oldenburg Hospital will be recruited shortly after surgical treatment. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient stay at the Geriatric Traumatology Center at Oldenburg Hospital due to proximal femur fracture
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to consent to the study
- Refusal to participate in the study
- Bed confinement prior to fracture event
- Polytrauma
- Complicative course with surgical revisions
- Isolated patients
